title: The expert pool A and B are plain tensors, not nn.Parameter, so no expert can ever train and every expert's contribution stays exactly zero for the whole run.
failure: Any run with FAB_ON=1. `pop.A`/`pop.B` are created by `torch.zeros(...)` with the default `requires_grad=False`. B is zero-init by design ("every expert is born an identity"), and because it receives no gradient it stays zero forever, so the expert contribution B(A(x)) is exactly 0.0 at step 0 and at step N. Verified: after `FAB.build(... d_model=16, signature_dim=8, rank=4 ...)`, `pop.A.requires_grad` -> False, `pop.B.requires_grad` -> False, `isinstance(pop.A, torch.nn.Parameter)` -> False, and `((x @ pop.A[0]) @ pop.B[0]).grad_fn` is None with output sum 0.0. The whole fabric is a permanent identity while the report prints n_live experts and a cull gate.
evidence: Body: `self.A = torch.zeros(cap, d_model, rank, device=device)` / `self.B = torch.zeros(cap, rank, d_model, device=device)` (fabric/api.py:66-67). Contract it contradicts: FAB.state_dict's frozen docstring enumerates them as parameters -- "Parameters (A, B, q_route, hproj, eemb, edec, halt_key, ...), the `cent` BUFFER" (fabric/api.py:695-696) -- and the Population docstring's "growth advances n_live into rows that are already there, so the optimizer NEVER SEES A NEW PARAMETER and a checkpoint's param-group structure survives a run that grew" (fabric/api.py:44-48) is only meaningful if the founding rows ARE parameters. `cent` being a plain tensor is correct; A and B are not.
fix: Wrap A and B as `nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(...))` (leave `cent` a buffer, as state_dict specifies) and hold them in an nn.Module (or register them on `pop.modules`) so they are reachable by the optimizer and by `pop.state_dict()`.

title: Population exposes no parameters(), so the router, the identity autoencoder and the halt head that build allocates never reach the optimizer either.
failure: Any run with FAB_ON=1. `spine/compose.py::_base_parameters` harvests the fabric with `params = getattr(obj, "parameters", None); if callable(params): out.extend(params())`. `Population.__slots__` defines no `parameters` and the class defines no such method, so the branch is skipped and the fabric contributes ZERO tensors to OPT's 'base' param group -- only a string appended to `sysm.warnings`. Verified: `hasattr(pop, 'parameters')` -> False while `sum(p.numel() for p in pop.modules.parameters())` -> 765 at (signature_dim=8, dk=6, emb_hid=12, d_model=16). q_route (the router), eemb/edec (the identity round-trip that ae_w and emb_var penalise) and halt_key (which decides every hop) are randomly initialised and then frozen for the entire run, so FAB_AE_W, FAB_EMB_VAR, FAB_HALT and every routing lever multiply a never-updated network.
evidence: `pop.modules = nn.ModuleDict({...}).to(device)` (fabric/api.py:173-179) assigns an nn.Module onto a __slots__ plain object (fabric/api.py:60-62), so nothing registers it in a module tree and no `parameters()`/`state_dict()`/`to()` surface exists. spine/compose.py:2116-2122 states the consequence in advance: "Population's declared fields (fabric/api.py::<module>) include no parameters() -- so if P4 does not add one, the fabric contributes ZERO parameters to the optimizer and every check in this tree stays green." P4 wrote the class and did not add one.
fix: Make Population hold an nn.Module (or add `def parameters(self): return itertools.chain([self.A, self.B], self.modules.parameters())`) so `_base_parameters` harvests A, B and the five shared modules; the warning path should then be a refusal rather than a note.

title: encode accepts n_layers and never uses it, so MEM's key-depth truncation is 100% inert -- the exact 'silently inert twice over' defect the docstring exists to end.
failure: MEM.key_depth is documented to arrive here as an argument so the memory-key path runs only the first n transformer blocks ("at LAYERS=12 the key path was paying twelve layers of attention over an 8-token window"). The body after the pos_max refusal never references `n_layers`: it always runs `model.body(h, ...)` in full. Verified on a 2-layer transformer (width 32, heads 4, ctx 8): `encode(..., n_layers=1)` and `encode(..., n_layers=0)` both differ from the full-stack output by max |dh| = 0.0. Consequence: the declared counter `lm.encode.key_path_truncated` can never be nonzero, MEM's key cost is whatever LM_LAYERS says, and the keys MEM stores are the full-depth hidden regardless of what key_depth is set to.
evidence: Signature `def encode(lm: Config, model, x, *, n_layers=None, extra=None)` (lm/api.py:397); body lines 449-461 contain no read of `n_layers`. Contract line contradicted: "n_layers runs only the first n blocks on the transformer arm, for the memory-key path (:1580-1593)... On the gru arm it is accepted and ignored, and that is a DECLARED GATE, not a silence -- CENSUS.md:250 records KEY_LAYERS as 'silently inert twice over'" (lm/api.py:415-421), plus "DID IT FIRE: ... lm.encode.key_path_truncated (n_layers actually reduced the stack)" (lm/api.py:432-433).
fix: On the transformer arm, when `n_layers` is not None, run only `model.body.layers[:n_layers]` (applying the same causal mask) and record `lm.encode.key_path_truncated`; on the gru arm record the declared unreachable Gate instead of silently ignoring the argument.

title: encode accepts `extra` and never adds it, so WORLD's forecast conditioning term is silently discarded.
failure: `extra` is documented as "an optional additive term on the hidden state, (B, L, width) or None" whose whole purpose is to let WORLD.forecast condition the LM as a parameter instead of monkey-patching model.encode. The body never adds it. Verified: `encode(cfg, m, x, extra=torch.ones(2,8,32))` differs from `encode(cfg, m, x)` by max |dh| = 0.0. WORLD's forecast therefore conditions on nothing while believing it does, the returned hidden (and every logit decoded from it) is the unconditioned one, and the declared counter `lm.encode.extra_applied` can never fire.
evidence: Signature `def encode(lm: Config, model, x, *, n_layers=None, extra=None)` (lm/api.py:397); the body at lines 449-461 is `e = ...; h = model.drop(e + pos); h = model.body(h, ...); return h` with no use of `extra`. Contract contradicted: lm/api.py:423-428 ("It exists so WORLD's forecast can condition the LM as a PARAMETER rather than by rebinding model.encode: the monkey-patch at :4158-4169 let a timing probe... A timing probe decided the run.") and lm/api.py:434 ("lm.encode.extra_applied").
fix: Add the term where the contract puts it -- on the hidden state, e.g. `h = h + extra` after the body (validating extra.shape == h.shape and extra.device == h.device) -- and set `lm.encode.extra_applied` when it is not None.

title: FAB.build initialises the shared modules AFTER moving them to the device, using a CPU generator -- RuntimeError on every RUN_DEVICE=cuda run.

title: The bigram arm returns an all-zero signature whenever width_units < 2, which is exactly the zero vector the contract says it may never return.

title: depth_now is hardcoded to 1 and FAB_DEPTH0 is never read at build, so the lever's documented 0 sentinel ('no curriculum') cannot be selected.

When the ByteComposer lands, LM_COMPOSE=1 will produce a strictly bias-free softmax while the banner and the checkpoint describe a decoder with a per-row bias, which shifts every logit and every reported bits/byte relative to the non-compose arm the numbers are compared against. title: SIG.encode does not run under no_grad despite its docstring, and the encoder is in the optimizer's param groups, so any caller's backward trains it
failure: SIG_MODE=learned (the default arm). The body has no torch.no_grad() anywhere: :186 returns `st.encoder(units.to(...))`, which builds an autograd graph through _Encoder.emb and _Encoder.proj. compose.py:1985-1987 puts those very parameters into the optimizer: `opt_api.build(opt, param_groups={..., "encoder": list(sig_api.encoder_parameters(sig, sysm.sig))}, ...)`. failure: Ran it: `WORLD_ENABLED=0 WORLD_HORIZON=0` returns the WORLD_HORIZON=0 refusal, and `WORLD_ENABLED=0 WORLD_HORIZON=999` against ctx_tokens=64 returns the horizon>=ctx refusal. compose.py raises on a non-empty refusal list before any tensor is allocated, so a legal configuration -- the null world, which build() constructs specifically so that "OFF is a configuration a run can actually take" -- is made unrunnable by a stale WORLD_HORIZON left in an operator's environment. Both refusals name a nan that a null world can never compute.
evidence: Docstring: "LEVERS READ: horizon, enabled". The body reads only `world.horizon` (line 402) and never `world.enabled`. Reasons given for both refusals are about the loss slices, which only the live world evaluates (build(): `if not bool(world.enabled): return World(built="null", ...)`).
fix: Open with `if not bool(world.enabled): return []`, or emit the two refusals as unreachable-with-reason gates on the disabled arm so the ledger still says why they could not fire.

title: encode adds the WINDOW count to sig.encode_calls and never produces sig.encode_windows, so the two documented counters collapse into one wrong number
failure: `st.counters["sig.encode_calls"] += int(units.shape[0])` adds N, not 1. Ran it: one call encoding 4 windows leaves `sig.encode_calls: 4`. The counters dict built in build() has no `sig.encode_windows` key, and SIG.counters(sig, st) is the only channel out, so the windows figure does not exist and the calls figure is really the windows figure. A reader computing windows-per-call, or checking that the encoder was queried once per flush, gets a number the run did not produce.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: sig.encode_calls, sig.encode_windows, and sig.encode_width_seen asserted equal to st.width_units on EVERY call". build() line 144 initialises `"sig.encode_calls": 0, "sig.train_steps": 0` and nothing else. Also: encode's "LEVERS READ: mode, d, bigram_dim" names three levers the body never reads (it reads st.mode, st.d and st.encoder.shape[0]), which is what lets K4 report them declared-and-read on prose alone.
fix: `counters["sig.encode_calls"] += 1` and `counters["sig.encode_windows"] += int(units.shape[0])`, initialising both in build(); record sig.encode_width_seen and correct encode's LEVERS READ line to "none directly -- everything comes off SigState".

title: the replay path neither reconciles the file's recorded settings nor distinguishes an unreadable parent vocabulary from a cold start
failure: `_replay_merges` reads only `blob["id2bytes"]` and drops every other key, so a resume launched with TOK_MIN_PAIR=200 against a parent built at 50 runs on the parent's table and prints nothing -- ISSUES P1-M80/L20 exactly, which the docstring cites as the thing this arm exists to fix. Separately, `_replay_merges` returns None when the file is missing and the body falls straight through to a fresh build: ran it with d_vocab_read_path="/nonexistent/parent.dyntok.json" and got a freshly minted 340-token vocabulary and no refusal, so the restored embedding table is indexed by a different vocabulary -- the failure the same paragraph says MUST NOT happen -- while CKPT.load raises loudly for the analogous missing checkpoint.
evidence: Docstring: "The file's recorded vmax/min_pair/max_tok/dropout DO NOT WIN: this package holds one declaration, the levers, and any disagreement is printed as a reconciliation line and counted" and "a resume MUST reuse the saved vocabulary or the restored embedding table is indexed by a different vocabulary". DID IT FIRE names `tok.load_reconciled`. Body: `replayed = _replay_merges(vocab, read_path); if replayed is not None: ...` with no else branch.
fix: Compare blob['min_pair'|'max_bytes'|'dropout'|'vmax'] against the resolved levers and emit one reconciliation line per disagreement with a tok.load_reconciled count; and raise when read_path is non-empty but unreadable, naming the path, instead of silently building a new vocabulary.

title: the declared Gate tok.build_passes_advice is never produced on any arm, so mode="fixed" runs silently at 2 passes where the build of record used 8
failure: The contract makes this a three-state gate that is never silent: on mode="fixed" it must print `build_passes=2; the offline build historically used 8 -- set TOK_BUILD_PASSES=8 to reproduce it`, and on the other two arms `unreachable (mode != fixed)`. The body creates no Gate at all -- tok/api.py does not even import spine.gate -- and there is no TOK counters() entry point and no counters/gates slot on Vocabulary, so there is no channel for it. An operator running mode="fixed" at the default build_passes=2 gets no statement that this is not the offline build of record, which the docstring flags as belonging on P9's list of numbers that moved.
evidence: Docstring: "The 8 is not lost: it is a DECLARED GATE with its predicate, tok.build_passes_advice ... Advice that appears sometimes and says nothing when it does not is armed-but-inert applied to prose." Imports at the head of tok/api.py: `from spine import derive as _derive` and `from spine import rng as _rng` -- no `Gate`. The same absence kills the other named surfaces here (tok.build_pass, tok.build_mint, tok.build_converged, tok.load_reconciled).
fix: Import spine.gate, carry a `gates`/`counters` slot on Vocabulary (or add TOK.counters), and emit Gate("tok.build_passes_advice", fired=(mode=="fixed"), value=build_passes, threshold=8, reachable=(mode=="fixed"), reason="mode != fixed").

title: n_by_name is counted and then discarded, so the declared data.phase_name_resolved surface cannot exist
failure: `n_by_name` is initialised at line 528, incremented at 548 for each schedule entry given as an area name, and never read again -- Plan carries only (protocol, schedule, phase_bounds, per_area_draw, exposure, gates) and DATA has no counters() entry point, so nothing can report it. The contract makes 0 a positive statement ("every entry was an index, which is the shipped spelling and a statement rather than silence"), and that statement cannot be made either way. A run launched with the Q-DATA-7 name spelling ("rust|rust|rust|rust") and one launched with "1|1|1|1" produce identical artifacts.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: data.phase_resolved, data.protocol_named ..., data.phase_name_resolved (entries given as a NAME rather than an index; 0 means every entry was an index ...)". `grep -n n_by_name src/data/api.py` returns exactly lines 528 and 548.
fix: Carry the counter out -- either as a field the root reads off Plan, or as a Gate in Plan.gates (Plan already has a gates tuple), and do the same for data.phase_resolved / data.protocol_named.

title: build declares norm_only, grow and halt in LEVERS READ but reads none of them, and no api.py body in the tree reads them either
failure: `grep -rn '\.norm_only\b|\.halt\b|\.grow\b' src/*/api.py` returns nothing. FAB.build is the only FAB entry point with a body, and it stores only `on` and `hop_arm` on the Population (`__slots__` has no norm_only/grow/halt) and records only fab.built/n0/cap/operating_population/off/hop_arm in pop.counters. So FAB_NORM_ONLY=1 -- a declared CONTROL ARM -- builds a Population byte-identical to FAB_NORM_ONLY=0, and nothing in any artifact this function produces says which arm ran. K4 passes on the prose, which is precisely the armed-but-inert shape it cannot catch.
evidence: Docstring: "LEVERS READ: on, norm_only, n0, slots, rank, dk, emb_hid, pressure, grow, halt, hop_mode". Body reads hop_mode, n0, slots, rank, on, dk, emb_hid, pressure and the d_operating_population wire, and nothing else. Verified by building at FAB_NORM_ONLY=1 FAB_GROW=0 FAB_HALT=0: counters are identical to the defaults apart from fab.off.

title: save_period declares a Gate for the dir-set/every==0 condition and produces none, so "the only saves are the final one plus SIGUSR1" is never stated
failure: The body returns a bare `U.Windows(int(ckpt.every))`. CKPT has no counters() entry point and no gate channel anywhere in the package (ckpt/api.py does not import spine.gate), so with CKPT_DIR set and CKPT_EVERY=0 -- the shipped default of `every` -- nothing anywhere tells the operator that periodic saving is off on a run that IS persisting. That is the :5619-5621 warning the contract asks to be replaced by a gate with its own condition, dropped rather than replaced.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: Cadences.ledger()[\"ckpt\"]; plus a declared Gate for the :5619-5621 warning -- dir set and every == 0 means the only save is the final one plus SIGUSR1, printed with its own condition rather than as a warning string." Line 126 is the whole body after owned_by.
fix: Return the period and expose the gate through a channel the root can read -- a package-level counters()/gates() accessor, or Gate("ckpt.periodic_armed", fired=(every>0), value=every, threshold=1, reachable=saving_on(ckpt), reason="CKPT_DIR is off: nothing is saved at all").

title: draw_stream passes again=True on every epoch stream with no rebuild to justify it, disarming the duplicate-stream guard
failure: "data.stream" is not in compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS, so nothing pre-mints `data.stream.e0` and there is no collision to work around -- the flag is pure suppression. With it, a second `draw_stream(epoch=0, seed=S)` anywhere in a process (a re-draw after a restore, a harness that redraws an epoch, the isolation sweep) silently gets a second generator replaying the first one's sequence instead of the RngError that exists to catch it. This is the same flag whose use in tokenize produced P1-H56 ("three regularize=True calls on one text produced ONE distinct segmentation").
evidence: `stream = _rng.rng_for(f"data.stream.e{int(epoch)}", seed, again=True)`. rng.py: "again=True if you are deliberately rebuilding this stream (checkpoint restore)". The call-site comment justifies determinism across seeds and epochs -- which the NAME already buys -- not a rebuild. compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS = ("lm","sig","fabric","memory","domains","world","tok.dropout","data.synth","data.holdout","eval").
fix: Drop again=True. If a legitimate rebuild is needed (a resume that re-draws the epoch it was interrupted in), pass it only on that path and say so at that call site.

title: load raises on a missing resume file and never constructs a Resume, so the attempted-without-loaded state the record exists for is unreachable
failure: Nothing in the package constructs `Resume`; `load` returns Snapshot or None and raises FileNotFoundError in between. The one state the record's own docstring says the old tree could not report -- "a RESUME that named a path nothing could be read from" -- is now a crash, and the run has no artifact that says attempted=True/loaded=False. resume_source's "DID IT FIRE: Resume.attempted" and load's "DID IT FIRE: Resume(attempted, loaded, step_restored, epoch_restored, best_restored)" have no producer, so step_restored/epoch_restored/best_restored are never reported either, even on a successful resume.
evidence: `@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True) class Resume: ... attempted: bool; loaded: bool; ...` with docstring "`attempted` without `loaded` is the state the old tree could not report"; `grep -n 'Resume(' src/ckpt/api.py` finds only the class definition. Body: `if not os.path.isfile(src): raise FileNotFoundError(...)` then `return Snapshot(...)`.
fix: Build and return/record the Resume alongside the Snapshot (attempted from resume_source, loaded/step/epoch/best from the blob), and keep the refusal as the loud arm -- the two are not exclusive, the record is what the report prints after the run survives.

title: open_areas reads dat.stream_bytes on the DEFAULT source arm while its LEVERS READ list omits it
failure: `_synthetic_areas` sizes each generated corpus as `max(seg_max+1, MIN_AREA_BYTES, stream_bytes // max(1, n)) * 2`, and DATA_SOURCE defaults to "synthetic", so on the shipped configuration DATA_STREAM_BYTES changes the generated corpus text -- and therefore the build sample, the merge table, the measured bytes_per_token and the derived signature width -- through an entry point whose contract says it does not read that lever. A reader auditing "which levers decide the corpus" from the frozen contract will not find it. The same list also omits nothing else, so it is not a blanket omission.
evidence: Docstring: "LEVERS READ: source, dir, areas, n_processes, corpus_cap, holdout_frac, val_cap, seg_max". Line 371: `per_area = max(int(dat.seg_max) + 1, MIN_AREA_BYTES, int(dat.stream_bytes) // max(1, n)) * 2`. Also note `max(1, n)` here is the silent clamp the project forbids: at DATA_N_PROCESSES=0 the body returns an Areas with names=() instead of refusing by name.
fix: Add stream_bytes to open_areas' LEVERS READ, and replace `max(1, n)` with a refusal naming DATA_N_PROCESSES and printing the value.

title: the UNREACHABLE arm of line() drops value and threshold even when the caller supplied them
failure: `data_plan` builds `Gate("data.exposure_skew_planned", False, None, float(dat.exposure_skew), reachable=False, reason=...)` -- the threshold is supplied -- and `line()` prints only "Gate data.exposure_skew_planned: UNREACHABLE -- a max/min ratio over ONE area is undefined". Confirmed the same way for fab.on at FAB_ON=0, where value=False and threshold=True are supplied and neither appears. A reader cannot see what the gate was armed at, which is the one thing the class docstring says the numbers are printed for.
evidence: Class docstring: "`value` and `threshold` are printed so the reader can do the arithmetic themselves. A gate that reports a verdict without the numbers behind it is a claim, and this project has paid for those." Body: `if not self.reachable: return f"Gate {self.name}: UNREACHABLE -- {self.reason}"` -- returns before the value/threshold branch.
fix: Append the supplied numbers on the unreachable arm too, e.g. `... UNREACHABLE ({value} vs {threshold}) -- {reason}` when either is not None.

title: the resample=False replay cache is keyed by id(areas), an address CPython reuses, so the stated per-Areas isolation does not hold and every Stream is retained forever
failure: `id()` is only unique among live objects. Demonstrated: after freeing one Areas, a newly built Areas landed on the same address within 134 allocations in the same interpreter -- exactly the isolation-sweep scenario the comment names. A stale entry from a freed run is then returned to a different run for any epoch>0 request that precedes that run's own epoch-0 draw. Independently, `_REPLAY` holds every Stream (bytes plus a per-byte labels list) for the life of the process with no eviction, so a sweep of many runs per interpreter leaks one full stream per run.
evidence: Comment above `_REPLAY`: "Keyed by the Areas object rather than by a module global holding one stream, so two Areas in one process (the isolation sweep runs many 200-step runs per interpreter) cannot hand each other's text back." Body: `_REPLAY[id(areas)] = st` and `cached = _REPLAY.get(id(areas))`.
fix: Cache on the Areas object itself (a mutable field the record already permits, like `cursors`) or use a `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`, so the entry dies with the Areas rather than outliving its address.

title: LMGeometry carries no record of whether the layer count came from the 0 sentinel, so lm.resolve.layers_from_sentinel cannot be reported
failure: `layers = _SENTINEL_DEPTH.get(arch, 1) if declared_layers == 0 else declared_layers` and LMGeometry stores only the resolved `layers`. A run at LM_ARCH=transformer LM_LAYERS=0 and one at LM_LAYERS=4 produce an identical LMGeometry and an identical geometry manifest, so the report cannot make the statement the contract asks for -- which number the run actually used -- even though that is the exact confusion ("a reader could not tell what depth a saved model was") the paragraph above it cites.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: lm.resolve.calls (must be exactly 1 per process), lm.resolve.layers_from_sentinel (1 when cfg.layers == 0 -- proves which number the run actually used)". LMGeometry fields: arch, width, layers, heads, ctx, pos_max, vocab_slots, compose, dropout, max_token_bytes, param_estimate.
fix: Add a `layers_from_sentinel: bool` (or the declared value beside the resolved one) to LMGeometry so LM.counters can report it, and count resolve() calls.

title: encode reads lm.ctx while declaring "LEVERS READ: none directly"
failure: The pos-overflow refusal interpolates `int(lm.ctx)` into its message, so encode does read an LM lever on the refusal path -- the one path where a reader most needs the contract to be accurate about where the number came from. The declared list says the function reads no lever directly, and the value it prints is a lever read rather than the wire it names in the same sentence.
evidence: Docstring: "LEVERS READ: none directly / WIRES READ: d_pos_max". Body line 445: `f"{pos_max} row(s) (LM_CTX={int(lm.ctx)} through the d_pos_max wire). Refused rather "`.
fix: Either name `ctx` in encode's LEVERS READ, or print only `d_pos_max` and let the wire ledger say where it came from.

title: the dead-row mask is rebuilt on every decode call although the contract specifies it is cached
failure: Every call allocates a bool tensor of vocab_slots, and when anything is retired also `torch.tensor(sorted(retired_ids))`, then a masked_fill -- once per window on the hot path, at LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=16384 with hundreds of retired ids on the probation arms. The documented cache key exists precisely because both inputs are monotone, so the rebuild is pure waste that the contract already ruled out.
evidence: Docstring: "The mask is cached on (live_vocab, len(retired_ids)); both only ever grow." Body lines 519-526 build `dead` and `idx` unconditionally on each call. The same docstring's "LEVERS READ: mask_dead_rows, vocab_slots, compose" also names two levers the body never reads (it uses model.compose and logits.shape[-1]).
fix: Memoise the mask on the model keyed by (live_vocab, len(retired_ids)) and reuse it, and correct the LEVERS READ line to the one lever actually read.

title: startup_refusals declares device and amp in LEVERS READ and reads neither
failure: The body reads only `run.epochs`. RUN_DEVICE and RUN_AMP are named as read by this entry point, which is what lets K4 report them covered on prose alone -- and clause (3) of the same docstring is a statement ABOUT amp and device ("amp != off with device == cpu is NOT refused") that the body cannot make, because it never looks at either value and returns no record saying the pair was considered.
evidence: Docstring: "LEVERS READ: epochs, device, amp" and "(3) amp != \"off\" with device == \"cpu\" is NOT refused: it is legal and inert, and Process.amp_state says so." Body lines 484-503 mention only `run.epochs` and the `disk_stream` argument.
fix: Drop device and amp from this list (Process.amp_state already carries the third state and process_setup declares both), or read them here to emit the not-refused case as an explicit unreachable gate.

title: The seg_contig cursor is advanced on a private copy and thrown away, so every epoch re-reads the identical head of every area and the exposure guard reports a number the run did not experience.
failure: DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_CORPUS_CAP=200000 DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 DATA_RESAMPLE=1 DATA_STREAM_BYTES=40000 RUN_EPOCHS=8. Measured: draw_stream(epoch=0/1/2) each return bytes exactly equal to bodies['eng'][:40000] (byte-identical, verified), and areas.cursors stays {'eng': 0} after every call. The run therefore sees 40,000 of the 190,000-byte body (21%) eight times and never sees the other 150,000 bytes, while data_plan's Gate data.exposure_max_planned prints 'armed, did not fire (1.6842 vs 2.0)'. Realized repetition on the material actually trained on is 8.0, i.e. 4x the guard's own threshold, and the guard exists precisely for P3-H22 ('py was memorised and eng was skimmed'). It also silently turns DATA_RESAMPLE=1 into the byte-identical-replay state the contract reserves for resample=False, with nothing reporting it.
evidence: Line 707 `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)` takes a COPY; line 729 `cursors[label] = start + want` writes only to the copy; the copy is never written back to `areas.cursors`, never returned on `Stream`, and `draw_stream` returns at line 751 discarding it. The docstring at lines 651-653 says the contiguous read comes "from a cursor that PERSISTS ACROSS EPOCHS, so an English-only run has only the text's own boundaries rather than discontinuities we manufacture every 8-20 KB", and `stream_state`'s docstring (lines 763-765) says "The cursors are LOAD-BEARING: without them a resume re-reads the head of every area under seg_contig and silently trains a second time on material the parent already used." The value it would checkpoint is permanently 0.
fix: Mutate `areas.cursors` in place (it is a plain dict on a frozen dataclass, which is why the field exists) rather than copying it -- `cursors = areas.cursors` -- or return the advanced cursors on `Stream` and have the composition root write them back. Store the cursor already reduced mod len(body) so the checkpointed value is bounded.

title: _replay_merges silently DROPS any saved entry that `_add` refuses and renumbers every id after it, so a resume attaches the parent's embedding rows to different tokens.
failure: Parent run at TOK_MAX_BYTES=32, TOK_SEED_VOCAB=4000, TOK_BUILD_PASSES=10 over data/train/{eng,py} builds 2565 ids, 4 of them longer than 16 bytes. Child resume at the default TOK_MAX_BYTES=16 with CKPT_RESUME=<parent>: `_add` returns None for those 4 (len(seq) > self.max_bytes), the child ends at 2561 ids, and from id 2556 onward every id means a different byte sequence than in the parent -- measured: parent[2556] = b':\n                ' vs child[2556] = b'raise '. LM.load_state then restores the parent's emb.weight/head.weight rows by index onto these renumbered tokens. No exception, no reconciliation line, no counter; the run continues and every logit for ids >= 2556 is attached to the wrong token. The same silent renumbering happens for any duplicate entry in the file and any entry refused by at_cap().
evidence: Line 309-310: `for seq_hex in blob.get("id2bytes", [])[256:]: vocab._add(bytes.fromhex(seq_hex), prov="replay")`. `_add` (line 129) returns None on `seq in self.seq2id or len(seq) > self.max_bytes or self.at_cap()` and the return value is discarded, while the new id is always `len(self.id2bytes)` (line 131) -- so a skip shifts every subsequent id by one. judge_probation's docstring (lines 562-564) states the invariant this breaks: "Ids are POSITIONAL -- merges[] is replayed in order and every later token is built on this one's index -- so removing an id would renumber the vocabulary and invalidate every checkpoint." build_vocabulary's docstring (lines 160-162) requires the opposite of silence: "a resume MUST reuse the saved vocabulary or the restored embedding table is indexed by a different vocabulary."
fix: Install replayed entries at their recorded index rather than by appending, and refuse loudly (naming the id, the recorded byte length, TOK_MAX_BYTES and the ceiling) when an entry cannot be installed -- a parent vocabulary that does not fit this run's caps is a resume that cannot be honoured, not one to truncate.

title: _replay_merges reads only a key called "id2bytes"; a vocabulary file in the `merges` format the contract says to write replays nothing and the resume silently trains with a 256-symbol byte vocabulary.
failure: Write the sidecar in the format save_vocabulary's docstring mandates and the only writer in this tree produces -- {"merges": [...], "vmax":..., "min_pair":..., "max_tok":..., "dropout":...}, i.e. exactly `tokenizer.py::ByteBPE.save` at line 473 -- and resume from it. Measured: build_vocabulary returns size=256, v0=256, bytes_per_token=1.0, with no exception and no warning. `blob.get("id2bytes", [])` is empty, the loop does nothing, `_replay_merges` still returns a truthy `vocab`, and line 241-245 takes the early return, SKIPPING the build entirely. The restored 4096-row embedding table is then indexed by a byte vocabulary that shares nothing with the parent's, and bytes_per_token=1.0 propagates into derive.signature_width_bytes and data_plan's splice gate. This is the exact failure the docstring exists to prevent.
evidence: Line 309 `blob.get("id2bytes", [])[256:]` versus save_vocabulary's docstring line 618: "Write merges plus the settings this run actually used". `_replay_merges` returns `vocab` unconditionally at line 311 whenever the path is a file, so build_vocabulary's guard `if replayed is not None` (line 241) cannot distinguish "replayed the parent" from "read a file it did not understand". Line 302 promises "Returns the vocabulary, or None if unreadable", but the only None is a missing path (line 305); a JSON parse error escapes instead -- verified: a truncated file raises json.decoder.JSONDecodeError out of build_vocabulary.
fix: Read the key the writer writes, and refuse loudly when the file carries no recognisable merge/vocabulary payload instead of returning a 256-id vocabulary: `raise` naming the path and the keys found. Wrap json.load so a corrupt file becomes the documented None or a named refusal, not a JSONDecodeError.

title: The resume path never mints `tok.dropout.mint`, so every resume with TOK_DROPOUT>0 dies in tokenize -- P1-H56's crash reintroduced on the branch the repair did not cover.
failure: CKPT_RESUME=<parent> with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3. Measured: build_vocabulary returns a Vocabulary with dropout_rng=None, and the very next row of the composition root (compose.py:1906, `tok_api.tokenize(..., regularize=True)`) raises ValueError('TOK.tokenize was asked to regularize with TOK_DROPOUT>0 against a Vocabulary carrying no dropout stream'). compose() cannot build the system at a supported lever value on any resume -- which is what P1-H56 records as "a supported lever value that could not build the system". Separately, `tok.dropout.mint` is ABSENT from rng.issued() on every resume, so the ledger cannot distinguish "declared and never asked" from "never existed" -- the three-state collapse G4 forbids.
evidence: Lines 240-245 return from the replay branch without ever executing line 260 `vocab.dropout_rng = _rng.rng_for("tok.dropout.mint", seed)`. The bytes arm at line 228 mints it deliberately with the comment "The stream is still minted so the ledger carries the key with zero draws -- DECLARED AND NEVER ASKED, which is a different statement from absent"; the replay arm does neither. tokenize lines 414-419 raise rather than segment without dropout.
fix: Mint `vocab.dropout_rng` immediately after constructing the Vocabulary (line 211), before any of the three return paths, so all four arms -- bytes, replay, fixed, online -- carry the stream.

title: bytes_per_token is measured on a dropout-free segmentation, but the frozen contract says it is measured WITH dropout applied -- so SIG's one signature width and DATA's splice gate use a number the training stream never produces.
failure: DATA_AREAS=eng,py, DATA_CORPUS_CAP=200000, TOK_DROPOUT=0.3. Measured: vocab.bytes_per_token = 1.7955 (the deterministic segmentation) while the segmentation the training stream actually consumes yields 1.5639 -- a 12.9% error. Downstream at LM_CTX=128, derive.signature_width_bytes gives 229 bytes instead of 200, so the domain encoder describes 14.5% more material than one loop stride covers, fixed for the lifetime of the run (the exact class of defect signature_width_bytes' own docstring records: "the domain encoder was reading 42% of the material it claimed to describe"). And the verdict of Gate data.splice_window flips: at DATA_SEG_MIN=1500/DATA_SEG_MAX=1900 it prints 'FIRED (7.397 vs 8.0)' on the reported value and 'armed, did not fire (8.492 vs 8.0)' on the value the run actually trains at.
evidence: Line 296 `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` then line 297 measures over those ids (same at line 243 on the replay path). tokenize's docstring, paragraph 2 (lines 391-396), is explicit: "bytes_per_token IS MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED. build_vocabulary measures it over the COUNTING segmentation, which applies tok.dropout, so more and shorter tokens lower it -- and derive.signature_width_bytes(LM.ctx, bytes_per_token) (SIG's one width) and data_plan's splice_window threshold both move with a TOK regularizer."
fix: Measure over a counting segmentation carrying the same dropout as the build passes: `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`, on both the build and replay paths.

title: A replayed vocabulary carries an EMPTY `merges` and `pair` table, so it is not the parent's vocabulary and the next save propagates the loss.
failure: Resume from a parent with 256 merges: measured `len(v2.merges) == 0` while `v2.size() == 512`. Three consequences follow with no error anywhere: restore_vocab's documented refusal ("REFUSE LOUDLY if the state's merge count does not match the vocabulary just built from the file") must fire on every honest resume, because the state records 256 and the vocabulary reports 0; save_vocabulary ("Write merges plus the settings this run actually used") writes an empty merge list, so a grandchild resume gets a 256-symbol byte vocabulary; and `vocab.pair` is empty, so nothing downstream can recover the (left_id, right_id) provenance the Mint/composer path is specified against.
evidence: Line 310 calls `vocab._add(bytes.fromhex(seq_hex), prov="replay")` with no `pair=` argument, and `_add` only appends to `self.merges` inside `if pair is not None` (lines 136-138). The module header (line 28) lists `merges` as part of the Vocabulary record; restore_vocab's docstring (line 716-717) makes the merge count the resume's refusal criterion.
fix: Recover each replayed sequence's constituent pair from the table built so far (the longest existing prefix/suffix split, or read the file's own `merges` list) and pass it as `pair=` so `merges` and `pair` reconstruct the parent's.

title: mode="fixed" closes the hard ceiling only on the build path; on a resume the ceiling is never closed, so a "fixed" vocabulary can keep minting.
failure: Same corpus, TOK_MODE=fixed. Build path: size=512, ceiling=512, at_cap()=True. Resume path (CKPT_RESUME=<parent>, parent of 600 ids): size=600, ceiling=4096, at_cap()=False -- the vocabulary is free to mint another 3496 ids on the one arm whose entire promise is "build to tok.seed_vocab as the CEILING as well as the target, then never mint". Every recorded fixed-arm resume is therefore not a fixed-arm run, and nothing says so.
evidence: Lines 279-290 (`if mode == "fixed": vocab.ceiling = vocab.size()`) sit AFTER the replay early-return at lines 241-245, so the replay branch never reaches them. This is P1-H57 ("the fixed arm's central promise at the mercy of an unrelated package's valve") repaired on one branch only.
fix: Apply the `mode == "fixed"` ceiling closure on the replay path too -- hoist it above the early return, or repeat it before line 245.

title: On the REAL path a zero-size held-out block is recorded with the reason "source=synthetic holds nothing out", and nothing refuses the configuration that produced it.
failure: DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng,py DATA_VAL_CAP=0 (or DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC=0.0, or any frac small enough that int(len(blob)*frac) == 0). Measured: every area comes back with hold=0 and rng_holdout = {'key': None, 'offset': 0, 'size': 0, 'seam_at': None, 'why': 'source=synthetic holds nothing out'} on a real disk corpus. The run has no held-out block at all -- the one number goal A and the across-the-run-boundary comparison rest on -- and the startup record states a false cause, so the operator cannot see which lever removed it. No refusal names DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC or DATA_VAL_CAP and no two numbers are printed, which is the project's stated rule for refusals.
evidence: Lines 287-310: the `if n_hold > 0` test is the only guard, and the `else` branch hard-codes `"why": "source=synthetic holds nothing out"` regardless of `dat.source`. `n_hold` is computed at line 276 as `min(int(len(blob) * float(dat.holdout_frac)), int(dat.val_cap))`, which is 0 for either lever at 0. The class docstring (lines 56-62) and the DID IT FIRE list name `data.val_cap_trip` and require `holdout` to be a real removed block.
fix: Branch on `str(dat.source) == "synthetic"` for the reason string, and on the real path raise CorpusError naming DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC, DATA_VAL_CAP, len(blob) and the resulting 0 when a real area's holdout rounds to zero.

title: A zero-length segment is recorded as a splice start and as an area change, and at DATA_SEG_MIN=DATA_SEG_MAX=0 the draw loop never terminates.
failure: DATA_SEG_MIN=0 DATA_SEG_MAX=3, two areas, 3000 bytes: measured 2021 splice_starts of which only 1509 are distinct (512 zero-length segments recorded as boundaries), and 206 of 1011 entries in `area_changes` point at an offset where labels[p] == labels[p-1] -- i.e. they are not changes at all. That is exactly the artefact `area_changes` exists to remove (P1-H10: "on a one-area run all ~96 'true switches' were artefacts"), reintroduced through the zero-length case, and boundary precision/recall scored against it is wrong. With DATA_SEG_MIN=0 DATA_SEG_MAX=0 the same path never terminates: `want` is always 0, `out` never grows, the `while len(out) < hi` loop spins forever appending to `splice` until memory is exhausted -- verified by a 20 s timeout with data_plan having already printed 'Gate data.splice_window: FIRED (0.0 vs 8.0)' and passed.
evidence: Line 717 `want = stream.randint(seg_min, seg_max)` can yield 0; line 720 can shrink it further; lines 733-741 append to `splice`, update `last_area` and append to `changes` unconditionally, before `out += chunk` adds nothing. Nothing in open_areas or data_plan refuses a seg_min below 1.
fix: Refuse DATA_SEG_MIN < 1 at startup in open_areas or data_plan, naming the lever and the value; and record the splice start / area change only after a non-empty chunk has been appended.

title: `again=True` is passed unconditionally to rng_for with no justification, disabling the one guard against two call sites sharing a stream name.
failure: The composition root's own tables call draw_stream twice for epoch 0 -- ASSEMBLY_ORDER's `stream` row (compose.py:1902, epoch=0) and LOOP_ORDER's `E` row (compose.py:687, epoch=clock.epoch, which is 0 on the first epoch). Two generators are therefore issued for `data.stream.e0` in one run, and `again=True` makes that silent. Any further consumer that asks for `data.stream.e<n>` -- a diagnostic, an eval replay, a future stratified draw -- receives a generator replaying DATA's exact sequence while believing it has its own, and neither RngError nor rng.issued() (which records one entry per name) can show it.
evidence: Line 702 `stream = _rng.rng_for(f"data.stream.e{int(epoch)}", seed, again=True)`; the comment above it (lines 698-701) explains the epoch-keyed NAME and says nothing about `again`. spine/rng.py's Rng.__init__ documents the flag as "a legitimate rebuild of one stream (checkpoint restore) passes again=True and says so at the call site", and the module header calls two call sites on one name "the thing this whole module removes".
fix: Drop `again=True`; if the root genuinely draws epoch 0 twice, have the second caller reuse the Stream (as the resample=False path already does) or call reset_issued() between runs. If a checkpoint-restore rebuild really needs it, pass it only on that path and say so in the comment.

title: The re-segmentation no-op refusal is absent: no invariant is stamped, so a re-tokenization whose match table has not moved is performed rather than refused, and tok.retok_noop can never be counted.
failure: tokenize is the single entry point for the initial segmentation, every in-loop re-segmentation, the final one and the held-out encode, and it holds no state whatsoever about the previous call. Calling it twice with an unchanged vocabulary performs the full segmentation again and returns a fresh Segmentation both times, with no way for any caller or report to tell a real retokenization from a no-op. The measured cost of not refusing is stated in the contract as 2.189 b/B and 68 points of word quality over 23 retoks of which 22 added zero tokens; that cost is fully reintroduced, and the three-state DID IT FIRE row tok.retok / tok.retok_noop collapses to one.
evidence: Lines 404-430 are the whole body: read dropout, pick the stream, `_segment`, map labels, return. The docstring at lines 365-369 requires the opposite: "A RE-SEGMENTATION WHOSE MATCH TABLE HAS NOT MOVED since the last one is REFUSED here and counted as tok.retok_noop, not performed ... The invariant stamped is (size, len(seq2id)) and NOT size alone, because retire() changes the match table without changing vocab_size." `Vocabulary.__slots__` (lines 74-76) carries no slot for the stamp, so P4 did not build the surface either.
fix: Add a stamp slot to Vocabulary, record (vocab.size(), len(vocab.seq2id)) on each segmentation, and when a caller asks for a re-segmentation at an unchanged stamp, return the previous Segmentation and count tok.retok_noop -- disabling the test whenever drop > 0, as the docstring requires.

title: The saved file's recorded settings are never read, so the documented reconciliation (tok.load_reconciled) and the tok.build_passes_advice Gate are mechanisms that cannot fire.
failure: A resume that sets TOK_MIN_PAIR=200 against a parent saved at min_pair=50 -- the case the docstring cites by id -- produces no reconciliation line, no counter and no difference in behaviour: the body reads nothing from the file except id2bytes, so the divergence between this run's declaration and the parent's recorded fact is invisible in exactly the way P1-M80/P1-L20 record ("the audit then printed 'NOTHING READ THESE' naming a knob that was set and ignored"). Likewise a TOK_MODE=fixed run at the default TOK_BUILD_PASSES=2 prints nothing saying it is not the offline build of record, because the Gate that was supposed to carry the retired literal 8 does not exist -- spine.gate is not even imported in this module and Vocabulary has no field to hang it on, so the Q-TOK-9 ruling's replacement for the number is silence.
evidence: Line 309 reads only `blob.get("id2bytes", ...)`; `vmax`, `min_pair`, `max_tok`, `dropout` are never touched, against the docstring at lines 160-164 ("The file's recorded vmax/min_pair/max_tok/dropout DO NOT WIN ... any disagreement is printed as a reconciliation line and counted") and lines 200-203 ("DID IT FIRE: ... tok.load_reconciled, Gate tok.build_passes_advice (fires on mode=\"fixed\" with the two numbers; 'unreachable (mode != fixed)' otherwise -- never silence)"). `grep Gate src/tok/api.py` finds only docstring text.
fix: Read the recorded settings, compare each against the resolved lever, and carry the disagreements plus the build_passes_advice Gate (from spine.gate) out on the Vocabulary so the report can print them.

title: On the synthetic path the operator's declared area names are silently replaced by p0..pN-1 whenever DATA_AREAS holds fewer entries than DATA_N_PROCESSES, and the label/key collision refusals are not applied at all.
failure: DATA_SOURCE=synthetic DATA_AREAS="e,p" DATA_N_PROCESSES=4: measured names ('p0','p1','p2','p3'). Every per-area score, the holdout rng keys and the across-the-run-boundary lookup then use labels that appear in no lever, and changing n_processes on a resume renames every area -- the desynchronised-label failure (P3-C19) this package exists to end. Separately, DATA_AREAS="x,x" or "a-b,a.b" on the synthetic path aborts with spine.rng.RngError("stream 'data.synth.a_b' was already issued") instead of the CorpusError naming both entries that the real path raises for the same condition, so the documented data.area_label_collision refusal is reachable on only one of the two sources.
evidence: Line 373 `labels = entries[:n] if len(entries) >= n else [f"p{i}" for i in range(n)]`; line 375 `_rng.rng_for(f"data.synth.{_holdout_key(label)}", seed)` with no prior collision check. open_areas performs the label and key collision refusals only inside the `else` (real) branch, lines 243-258. DATA_AREAS is declared as "The corpora to stream, in order; their names label every per-area score in the report and across the run boundary" (data/levers.py:241).
fix: Run the same label and key collision refusals over the synthetic labels before any rng_for call, and refuse (naming DATA_AREAS and DATA_N_PROCESSES with both counts) when the two disagree rather than inventing p0..pN-1.

title: DATA_SEG_MIN > DATA_SEG_MAX passes every startup gate and then dies inside the draw with a bare ValueError that names no lever.
failure: DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_SEG_MIN=2000 DATA_SEG_MAX=1800: open_areas succeeds (its floor is derived from seg_max alone, max(1801, 5000)), data_plan succeeds and prints 'Gate data.splice_window: armed, did not fire (16.493 vs 8.0)' computed from a mean segment of 1900 bytes that no draw can ever produce, and only then draw_stream raises ValueError('empty range for randrange() (2000, 1801, -199)'). The operator gets a stdlib message naming neither DATA_SEG_MIN nor DATA_SEG_MAX nor their values, after a gate has already reported an arithmetic result about a distribution that does not exist.
evidence: Line 717 `want = stream.randint(seg_min, seg_max)` with no ordering check; line 216 `floor = max(int(dat.seg_max) + 1, MIN_AREA_BYTES)` reads only seg_max; line 632 `mean_seg = (int(dat.seg_min) + int(dat.seg_max)) / 2.0` computes a mean over an empty range. The project rule is that a refusal names the lever and prints both numbers.
fix: Refuse at the top of data_plan (or open_areas) when seg_min > seg_max, naming DATA_SEG_MIN and DATA_SEG_MAX and printing both values; derive the area floor from max(seg_min, seg_max) + 1.

title: `seam_at` is recorded as the block offset unconditionally, so a block at offset 0 or at the tail reports a manufactured seam that does not exist -- the unreachable state the contract requires it to say.
failure: When the drawn `start` is 0 the removal takes a prefix and leaves no manufactured discontinuity, yet the record reads seam_at: 0, which a report renders as a seam at position 0. When start + n_hold == len(blob) the removal takes the tail and again leaves no seam, yet the record reads seam_at: start -- an offset that is the END of the body. Either way the data.holdout_seam reading counts a discontinuity the body does not contain, and DATALevers' claim that the only boundaries left under seg_contig are the text's own is checked against a number that is wrong in exactly the two cases where the claim is true.
evidence: Line 305 `rng_holdout[label] = {..., "seam_at": start}` with no test on start or start + n_hold. The DID IT FIRE list at lines 189-194 requires the opposite: data.holdout_seam is "Unreachable when a block lands at offset 0 or at the tail, which is the state it must say rather than read 0".
fix: Set `"seam_at": start if 0 < start and start + n_hold < len(blob) else None`, with a `why` naming which of the two boundary cases applies, so the report can print UNREACHABLE rather than a position.

title: data.holdout_overlap is never computed, so the one instrument declared for near-duplicate contamination between the held-out block and the training body produces no number at all.
failure: The contract makes the overlap a per-area reading printed once at startup and states why the split rule alone cannot answer it (Lee et al. arXiv:2107.06499: models "underestimate perplexity on evaluation documents with near duplicates", so "NEITHER the tail nor the random block is safe on its own"). open_areas computes nothing of the kind and `Areas` carries no field for it -- `rng_holdout` holds key/offset/size/seam_at only. A run on data/train/eng, whose seven files include dracula.txt while data/continual/03_dracula exists as a separate area, has no way to report that its held-out English overlaps its training material, and every held-out b/B figure the project publishes is uncontrolled for it.
evidence: Lines 211-316 contain no n-gram or overlap computation; the returned Areas fields are fixed at lines 64-71. The DID IT FIRE list at lines 195-202 declares data.holdout_overlap as "a READING, not a lever and not a gate: the fraction of held-out bytes that also occur verbatim in the training body at a fixed n-gram length, per area, printed once at startup. It costs no lever, no wire and no default, and it answers the one question the split rule CANNOT".
fix: Compute the fraction of held-out bytes covered by n-grams (fixed length, e.g. 50) that also occur in bodies[label], and carry it per area on rng_holdout so the startup banner can print it beside the offset and size.
